title: Auto-stop the session when the lid closes
description: Detect clamshell (lid-closed) transitions via IOPMrootDomain's AppleClamshellState and stop an active caffeinate session when the laptop enters clamshell mode. Needs a Settings window to host the preference (default on), and must degrade gracefully on hardware/OS that doesn't publish the key (desktop Macs).
acceptance_criteria: Open->closed transition stops an active session when the preference is on; no action when off, when no session is running, or when the state is unavailable; Settings window exposes the toggle and explains unsupported hardware.
close_reason: Verified on hardware: two lid closes, both detected via IOKit notification, caffeinate child reaped each time. Confirmed the notification arrives before system sleep as well as on a docked/no-sleep close.

title: Login-item guard fails when the old bundle is briefly absent
description:
LoginItemPolicy uses recordedBundleExists to avoid hijacking another copy's login item. During a 'brew upgrade' the old bundle is removed before the new one lands, so a stray launch from a different path during that window sees recordedBundleExists=false and takes the registration.

Hit live: brew's 'Reopening 1 application' relaunched the repo-path build while /Applications/Espresso.app was momentarily gone. Final state recovered because the /Applications copy launched afterwards and re-adopted, but a duplicate BTM record for the repo path may persist.

Consider requiring the app to be running from a stable location, or confirming absence over a short delay, before treating a missing bundle as 'the app moved'.
close_reason: Re-registration now also requires the running bundle to be in an Applications directory, so a build or download can't claim the item mid-upgrade

title: Activate public distribution: tap repo, TAP_TOKEN, first release
description:
Everything is built and CI-verified; these are the outward-facing steps left, all requiring account-level actions.

1. gh repo edit panchr/espresso --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences
2. gh repo create panchr/homebrew-tap --public --add-readme --description 'Homebrew tap for panchr'
3. Fine-grained PAT scoped to homebrew-tap with Contents: read+write, then: gh secret set TAP_TOKEN
4. git tag v0.1 && git push origin v0.1

Step 4 publishes the release and pushes the stamped cask. Without step 3 the release still succeeds and the tap step is skipped with a notice. First release is v0.1 (pre-1.0); verified the two-component tag stamps the bundle and orders correctly in Homebrew.
design: Cask installs prebuilt artifacts only, so GitHub releases stay the distribution unit; the cask is a checksum-stamped pointer at them.
close_reason: Repo public, v0.1 released, tap created and cask published; only the CI automation token remains

title: Prepare repo for public release + one-line installer
description: Make the repo publishable: license, CI, tagged release workflow that builds a universal Espresso.app, and a curl-able install.sh so users can install without a Swift toolchain.
close_reason: Release plumbing, installer, and docs landed; repo stays private for now

title: Add TAP_TOKEN so releases auto-update the Homebrew cask
description:
The v0.1 cask was pushed to panchr/homebrew-tap by hand. Until TAP_TOKEN exists, every future release needs that manual push.

Setup: create a fine-grained PAT scoped to panchr/homebrew-tap with Contents: read+write, then in the espresso repo run: gh secret set TAP_TOKEN

The release workflow picks it up automatically on the next tag. To publish the cask for an already-tagged release: gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=vX.Y
close_reason: Solved with an SSH deploy key (TAP_DEPLOY_KEY) instead of a PAT; verified end to end by dispatching the workflow against v0.1
